facts.fact: Free legal aid is provided by the Legal Services Authorities to those covered by Section 12 of the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987
facts.quote: Legal Services includes providing Free Legal Aid to those weaker sections of the society who fall within the purview of Section 12 of the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987.

facts.fact: Free legal aid includes representation by an advocate and payment of process fees and other court charges
facts.quote: Provision of free legal aid may include: Representation by an Advocate in legal proceedings. Payment of process fees, expenses of witnesses and all other charges payable or incurred in connection with any legal proceedings in appropriate cases;

facts.fact: Free legal aid includes drafting of legal documents and supply of certified copies of judgments and orders
facts.quote: Drafting of legal documents, special leave petition etc. Supply of certified copies of judgments, orders, notes of evidence and other documents in legal proceedings.

facts.fact: Legal services include giving advice on any legal matter (Section 2(c))
facts.quote: “legal services” includes any service in the conduct of any case or other legal proceeding before any court or other authority or tribunal and the giving of advice on any legal matter.

facts.fact: There is no charge for getting or submitting the legal aid application form
facts.quote: No, there is absolutely no charge for getting or submitting an application form for free legal aid.

facts.fact: Process, drafting and typing fees and the panel lawyer's fees are borne by the legal services institutions, so the aid is completely free
facts.quote: No, expenses like Process Fees, Drafting Fees, Typing Fees, Clerkage as well as Fees of panel lawyers (during or after the case is completed) are borne by the legal service institutions.

facts.fact: Eligible under Section 12: SC/ST members, victims of trafficking or begar, women and children, and persons with mental illness or disability
facts.quote: A member of a Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe; A victim of trafficking in human beings or begar as referred to in Article 23 of the Constitution; A woman or a child; A mentally ill or otherwise disabled person;

facts.fact: Also eligible: victims of mass disaster, ethnic violence, caste atrocity, flood, drought, earthquake or industrial disaster, and industrial workmen
facts.quote: A person under circumstances of undeserved want such as being a victim of a mass disaster, ethnic violence, caste atrocity, flood, drought, earthquake or industrial disaster; or An industrial workman;

facts.fact: Also eligible: persons in custody, including in a protective home, a juvenile home or a psychiatric hospital
facts.quote: In custody, including custody in a protective home within the meaning of clause (g) of Section 2 of the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956(104 of 1956); or in a juvenile home within the meaning of clause(j) of Section 2 of the Juvenile Justice Act, 1986 (53 of 1986); or in a psychiatric hospital

facts.fact: Also eligible: persons with annual income below the State-prescribed ceiling for cases in courts other than the Supreme Court, and below Rs 5 lakh for Supreme Court cases
facts.quote: or a person in receipt of annual income less than the amount mentioned in the following schedule (or any other higher amount as may be prescribed by the State Government), if the case is before a Court other than the Supreme Court, and less than Rs 5 Lakh, if the case is before the Supreme Court.

facts.fact: A woman is eligible for free legal aid irrespective of her income
facts.quote: Yes, a woman is entitled for free legal aid irrespective of her income or financial status.

facts.fact: A child is eligible for free legal aid till 18 years of age
facts.quote: A child is eligible for free legal aid till the age of majority i.e. 18 years.

facts.fact: An affidavit of income is generally sufficient proof of income (Section 13(2))
facts.quote: As per Section 13(2) of the Act, an affidavit made by a person as to his income is generally regarded as sufficient for making him/her eligible for the entitlement of legal services under the Act

facts.fact: The Legal Services Authority must be satisfied that the person has a genuine case to prosecute or defend
facts.quote: any individual who satisfies any criteria under Section 12 is entitled to receive legal services, provided that the concerned Legal Services Authority is satisfied that such person has a genuine case to prosecute or defend the matter.

facts.fact: NALSA's two pages give different State income ceilings for some States: the legal-aid page lists Jammu & Kashmir at Rs 3,00,000 a year
facts.quote: 10. Jammu & Kashmir Rs. 3,00,000/- 11. Jharkhand Rs. 3,00,000/-

facts.fact: NALSA's two pages give different State income ceilings for some States: the FAQ page lists Jammu & Kashmir at Rs 1,00,000 a year
facts.quote: 10. Jammu & Kashmir Rs.1,00,000/- 11. Jharkhand Rs.3,00,000

facts.fact: NALSA helpline 15100 is toll-free, for urgent legal assistance
facts.quote: One can directly contact on NALSA Helpline Toll-Free Number 15100 to seek urgent legal assistance.

facts.fact: Apply at the Taluk Legal Services Committee (in the court premises of the Taluk) or the District Legal Services Authority (in the District Court premises)
facts.quote: Taluk Legal Services Committee which is in the premises of the Court in that Taluk; or District Legal Services Authority which is in the premises of the District Court in the District Headquarters;

facts.fact: For High Court or Supreme Court cases, apply to the High Court Legal Services Committee or the Supreme Court Legal Services Committee
facts.quote: The High Court Legal Services Committee which is in the premises of the concerned High Court; or The Supreme Court Legal Services Committee for cases before the Hon’ble Supreme Court.

facts.fact: Each DLSA, High Court Legal Services Committee and SLSA has a front office where the application can be made
facts.quote: Each District Legal Services Authority, High Court Legal Services Committee and State Legal Services Authority has a front office where an application can be moved.

facts.fact: The ready-made application form can be submitted in person at the Authority or sent by post
facts.quote: You can fill up the ready-made form/application form that is available at your nearest Legal Services Authority and submit the same at either the Authority physically, or post the application to the Authority.

facts.fact: A plain-paper application can be made with name, address, employment status, SC/ST proof if any, income with affidavit and the case for which aid is needed
facts.quote: You can even make an application in writing on a simple piece of paper with the necessary details such as your name, gender, residential address, employment status, nationality, whether SC/ST (with proof in support), income per month (with affidavit), the case for which legal aid is required

facts.fact: The plain-paper application also gives the reason for seeking legal aid and can be submitted in person or by post
facts.quote: the case for which legal aid is required, reason for seeking legal aid, etc. and submit it physically or send by post.

facts.fact: The application can be sent by email to NALSA at nalsa-dla@nic.in or through the online application form on NALSA's website
facts.quote: Another option is to send the application online i.e. by email to NALSA (at nalsa-dla@nic.in), or through the online application form available online at NALSA’s website

facts.fact: nalsa.gov.in links a 'Legal Aid Application' e-service
facts.quote: e-Services Legal Aid Application Victim Compensation Application LSMS Portal LACMS Portal NALSA Helpline Number 15100

facts.fact: The online Legal Aid application is NALSA's Legal Services Management System (scourtapp.nic.in/lsams), with 'Apply Legal Aid' and application tracking
facts.quote: National Legal Services Authority Legal Services Management System Now citizens can also track their applications

facts.fact: An application can also be made orally; a paralegal volunteer or an officer of the Legal Services Authority assists
facts.quote: It is also possible to make your application orally – a paralegal volunteer or an officer of the concerned Legal Services Authority will assist you in such cases.

facts.fact: Once the application is accepted, a lawyer is assigned and the applicant is informed
facts.quote: Once the application is selected, the applicant is given intimation about the assignment of a lawyer.

facts.fact: The applicant may name a panel lawyer of choice; the Member-Secretary or Secretary can consider and allow it (not mandatory)
facts.quote: if the applicant has mentioned/expressed his/her choice of a lawyer on the panel, such Member-Secretary or Secretary can consider and allow the same.

summary: All claims confirmed on nalsa.gov.in (legal-aid and FAQ pages), home page and LSAMS; the two NALSA pages still give different State ceilings (e.g. J&K Rs 3 lakh vs Rs 1 lakh).
